title: Multichannel Marketing Data Model Architecture
summary: The MCM (Multichannel Marketing) data model defines the entity relationships for orchestrating customer engagement across multiple channels. The model includes approximately 40+ entities organized into three layers: CRM-shared entities (territory, sales rep, product), MCM-shared entities (HCO, Contact Master), and MCM-custom entities (journey metadata, consent management, channel preferences).

findings.customer_master_entities: Contact Master serves as the central hub with specialized extensions: ContactHCP (profession, specialty, license, certification, practice location cross-references), Contact Consumer, and HCO (healthcare organization) with brick cross-references and address management. ContactHCO junction enables many-to-many HCP-to-organization relationships.
findings.consent_and_preference_model: Consent is tracked per channel per contact: Physical Address Current Consent, Email Current Consent, and Phone Current Consent — each with audit trail. Contact Channel Preference records the preferred communication channel per contact. Consent Audit maintains the full history of opt-in/opt-out events.
findings.journey_orchestration_entities: Journey MetaData defines the orchestration templates. Topic and Topic Communication Channel Xref control which channels are valid for each communication topic. These entities enable channel-aware message routing.
findings.territory_and_product_model: Territory and SalesRep entities are shared from CRM. Product Master includes therapeutic area and brand hierarchy. The model supports territory-based access control for MCM campaigns.
findings.entity_color_coding: The data model uses three color-coded entity categories: Orange for custom MCM entities (journey, consent, preferences), Purple for entities shared from CRM (territory, sales rep, product), and Blue for entities shared from MCM platform (HCO, contact master).

source: MCM Data Model V12 ER diagram
